To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular signatures of follicular neoplastic nodules are characterized by a strong enrichment in transcripts encoding proteins associated with cell proliferation, a depletion of transcripts encoding factors that induce cell cycle arrest or apoptosis, and a strong enrichment of transcripts encoding proteins involved with cell migration.
the molecular signature of FC is enriched in genes encoding proteins involved in the cell cycle and depleted in genes encoding proteins that are involved in the control of cell cycle and apoptosis.

the transcriptome of follicular thyroid carcinomas is characterized by a strong enrichment of transcripts encoding proteins involved mitosis and DNA replication, whereas those involved in growth arrest or apoptosis are depleted, which provides an accurate and robust molecular signature for the differential diagnosis of follicular adenomas and carcinomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of thyroid neoplasia with a particular focus on the diagnosis of follicle-derived tumors.
the identification and characterization of molecular pathways leading to follicular thyroid neoplasia.
the identification and validation of molecular signatures of FC and FA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the molecular signatures described here provide an important tool to improve our knowledge of the molecular pathogenesis of follicular thyroid tumors as well as to provide an accurate diagnostic tool for the classification of follicular neoplastic lesions.

the molecular pathways leading to FC are characterized by an increased rate of cell proliferation, which is associated with a loss of the ability to induce growth arrest and apoptosis, and the latter is associated with a down-regulation of NR4A family members.

the analysis of the transcriptome signatures of FC and FA provided a molecular pathway that is likely to play a role in the pathogenesis, and the molecular signatures of the tumors could be exploited for a robust and accurate diagnosis of follicular neopplasias.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to identify a molecular signature for follicular neoplastic lesions of the thyroid gland that can distinguish between follicular adenoma and follicular carcinoma.
we identified molecular pathways that are involved in thyroid carcinogenesis, and we generated an accurate classifier that could be used in the future to diagnose FA and FC.

our study provides a comprehensive molecular signature of follicular thyroid neoplasia and that the results may provide a molecular basis for understanding and diagnosis of follicular thyroid nodules.

the analysis of the transcriptome of follicular neoples provides leads to their diagnosis, which may be exploited in the future for molecular diagnostics.

the molecular signatures of thyroid follicle neoplasia can be used to identify carcinomas and that the analysis of differentially regulated genes provides a mechanistic insight into the pathogenesis of thyroid carcinomas.
